overview: September 14-15 saw active development across twelve bpf-next patch series covering kfuncs, JIT backends, and tooling. Highlights include new kfuncs for RCU callbacks and user memory access via mm_struct, BPF-driven proactive memcg reclaim, and CPUv4 instruction extensions for the i386 JIT.

patches.title: bpf: Add user memory access kfuncs for mm_struct
patches.author: Anastasios Papagiannis
patches.summary: This 5-patch series (v7) adds kfuncs that allow BPF programs to read strings from a remote process's virtual address space via its mm_struct. A new mm helper copy_remote_mm_str() is introduced, and linux_binprm->mm is annotated as trusted-or-null so the verifier accepts it as a kfunc argument. The exec path is also fixed to clear bprm->mm before dropping its reference, closing a potential use-after-free window. This is particularly useful for tracing programs that need to inspect the address space layout or argument strings of an execve-ing task.

patches.title: bpf: Add bpf_call_rcu() kfunc
patches.author: Puranjay Mohan
patches.summary: This 4-patch series (v2) introduces bpf_call_rcu() and bpf_call_rcu_tasks_trace() kfuncs, enabling BPF programs to schedule callbacks to run after an RCU grace period, analogous to the kernel's call_rcu() and call_rcu_tasks_trace() APIs. This allows deferred, safe memory reclamation and cleanup for BPF programs that operate on RCU-protected kernel data structures. Selftests for both kfuncs are included in the series.

patches.title: mm/bpf: Add bpf_proactive_reclaim kfunc
patches.author: Hui Zhu
patches.summary: This 2-patch series (v11) adds a bpf_proactive_reclaim kfunc that lets BPF programs trigger proactive memory reclaim for a specific memcg cgroup. It enables policy-driven or tracing-controlled memory pressure management without requiring a dedicated kernel thread. The lengthy revision history reflects significant review on the safety semantics of triggering reclaim from a BPF context; the accompanying selftest verifies async reclaim behavior.

patches.title: bpf, x86: Add support for BPF_MOVSX in the i386 JIT
patches.author: Nicholas Dudar
patches.summary: This 5-patch series extends the x86 32-bit (i386) JIT compiler to support CPUv4 BPF instructions. Individual patches add BPF_MOVSX (sign-extending moves), BPF_MEMSX (sign-extending memory loads), BPF_JMP32|BPF_JA (unconditional 32-bit jumps), and unconditional byte swaps, preceded by a refactor to extract a shared load emitter. These additions bring the i386 JIT to feature parity with modern BPF instruction set requirements.

patches.title: bpf: Fix generic __uninit kfunc output buffers
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This 3-patch series (v1) fixes a verifier bug where the generic kfunc argument handling path did not properly recognize and initialize output buffers annotated with __uninit. Without the fix, the verifier could incorrectly reject or mishandle kfuncs that declare uninitialized output buffers, leading to false rejections of valid programs. A selftest for privileged capability test preparation is also included.

patches.title: libbpf: support selective kernel module BTF loading via bpf_object_open_opts
patches.author: Fuyu Zhao
patches.summary: This 2-patch series (v9) adds a new field to bpf_object_open_opts that lets callers specify which kernel module BTFs should be loaded during BPF object open, skipping all others. On systems with many modules, eager BTF loading is a measurable overhead; this opt-in filtering reduces load latency for programs that only use types from a small set of modules. Selftests validate the selective loading behavior.

patches.title: xsk: Fix circular locking dependency between &net->xdp.lock, &xs->mutex, and netdev_lock_ops
patches.author: Khawar Ahemad
patches.summary: This single patch (v6) resolves a lockdep-reported circular dependency among the XDP namespace lock, the AF_XDP socket mutex, and netdev lock ops in the xsk socket path. The fix restructures acquisition order to eliminate the cycle, which could otherwise cause deadlocks under concurrent socket operations and device configuration changes. Six revisions indicate the locking restructuring required careful review to avoid introducing new races.

patches.title: bpftool: Compute map size of light skeletons at runtime
patches.author: Leon Hwang
patches.summary: This standalone patch (v2) fixes bpftool's light skeleton code generation to compute BPF map sizes dynamically at runtime rather than embedding statically computed values. Static sizes can become stale or incorrect when the underlying map definitions change or differ between kernel versions. The runtime computation ensures generated skeletons remain correct across kernel variants.
